DILG Republic of the Philippines r r rvc DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, Quezon City www.dilg.gov.ph DILG OPINION No. 42 s. 2021 12 March 2021 VICE-MAYOR NORMAN L. LACSON Office of the Sangguniang Bayan Municipality of Magalang Province of Pampanga Dear Vice-Mayor Lacson: This has reference to your letter dated 3 January 2021 requesting for a legal opinion on the implication of an inaction!action of the Local Chief Executive of the Ordinance concerning the annual budget of the Local Government Unit (LGU). Specifically, the query is herein below quoted: The Annual Budget for Fiscal Year 2021 of the LGU of Magalang was approved by tho Sangguniang Bayan thru Appropriation Ordinance No. 4, s. 2020 which was transmitted to the Municipal Mayor for his approval. The LCE returned said Appropriation Ordinance with a veto message vetoing items in the MOOE and Capital outlay of the Office of the Municipal Vice Mayor and the the Office of the Sangguniang Bayan. Said veto was not overridden by the Sangguniang Bayan due to insufficient number of votes to satisfy the 2/3 requirement of the law. We seek to be clarified if the Office of the Vice Mayor and the Sangguniang Bayan will operate on re-enacted budget on the line items vetoed by the Municipal Mayor. All copies of the Appropriation Ordinance authorizing the Annual 2. Budget of the LGU of Magalang, Pampanga for FY 2021 enacted by the Sangguniang Bayan which were transmitted to the Local Chief Executive for his signature were returned back to the Office of the Sangguniang Bayan along with the veto message 8 days after these were received by his office but without affixing his signature on any page and on any copy of the appropriation ordinance. To date, the LGU of Magalang, Pampanga does not have a duly signed appropriation ordinance enacting the Annual Budget for FY 2021. This is not to be deemed approved as it was returned within IO day prescriptive period for his approval. We therefore humbly seek clarification from the DILG on the implication of such inaction/action of the Municipal Mayor on the status of the Annual Budget of the LGU of Magaiang, Pampanga for FY 2021. "

The queries shall be answered simultaneously as they revolve around the same subject matter. The governing law is Section 54 of R.A. No. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991 ". To wit: "SECTION 54. Approval of Ordinances. — (a) Every ordinance enacted by the sangguniang panlalawigan, sangguniang panlungsod, or sangguniang bayan shall be presented to the provincial governor or city or municipal mayor, as the case may be. If the local chief executive concerned approves the same, he shall affix his signature on each and every page thereof: otherwise, he shall veto it and return the same with his objections to the sanggunian, which may proceed to reconsider the same. The sanggunian concerned may override the veto of the local chief executive by two-thirds (2/3) vote of all its members, thereby making the ordinance or resolution effective for all legal intents and purposes. (b) The veto shall be communicated by the local chief executive concerned to the sanggunian within fifteen (15) days in the case of a province, and ten (IO) days in the case of a city or a municipality; othetwise, the ordinance shall be deemed approved as if he had signed it. " The above cited provision did not include signature of the Local Chief Executive as a requirement in order for a veto to be valid. As specified, the veto shall be made by returning the appropriations ordinance accompanied with his objections thereon within the prescribed period. In the facts presented, the appropriations ordinance was returned by the Municipal Mayor with a veto message containing his objections on some of the items. In fact, the Department in its Legal Opinion No. 72, Series of 2019 has opined that the word "veto" need not be written in the originai copy of the proposed ordinance itself. The veto power of the Mayor is complete and duly exercised when he communicated his written veto message to the Sanggunian coupled with the act of returning the proposed ordinance unsigned. Hence, we opine that the same is a valid veto which calls for the application of Section 323 of the Local Government Code of 1991 which partly states as follows: . — In case the SECTION 323. Failure to Enact the Annual Appropriations sanggunian concerned fails to pass the ordinance authorizing the annual

appropriations at the beginning of the ensuing fiscal year, it shall continue to hold sessions, without additional remuneration for its members, until such ordinance is approved, and no other business may be taken up during such sessions. !f the sanggunian still fails to enact such ordinance after ninety (90) days from the beginning of the fiscal year, the ordinance authorizing the appropriations of the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted and shall remain in force and effect until the ordinance authorizing the proposed appropriations is passed by the sanggunian concerned. However, only the annual appropriations for salaries and wages of existing positions, statutory and contractual obligations, and essential operating expenses authorized in the annual and supplemental budgets for the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted and disbursement of funds shall be in accordance therewith. It follows, therefore, that the LGU concerned shall operate on a reenacted budget insofar as the vetoed items are concerned. Clearly, therefore the operation on a reenacted budget is not a mere implication of the veto made by the Locai Chief Executive, it appiies by operation of law. Notwithstanding the foregoing discussion, this opinion is being rendered without prejudice to final and authoritative determination of the issues by competent courts. We hope to have guided you on the matter. Thank you. Very truly yours, By Au ority of the Secretary: MA NGAN, CESO Ill fficer n-Charge Office of the Undersecretary for Local Government LLLS/84 Copy furnished: DIRECTOR JULIE J.
